I analyze divergence between independent signals to detect coercion where the actors involved can manipulate what data is recorded. Previous cases include a single agroindustrial firm in coastal Honduras, the national government of Afghanistan, opium cultivation under competing armed groups in northern Myanmar, and soil degradation along a displacement corridor in eastern Cameroon. I've worked eight years in teaching, social work, manual labor, and program design across Africa, Asia, Latin America, and the American South, including co-founding a teacher-training program in Egypt (2017–present) and developing cybersecurity curricula and training for USAID in Kazakhstan (2021). Hablo español.
